questions.question: Change to the passive voice: The board will announce the results.
options: The results are announced by the board.
The results would announce by the board.
The results have been announced by the board.
The results will be announced by the board.
questions.explanation: Future active becomes "will be + past participle".

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: She has written the letter.
options: The letter has been written by her.
The letter was written by her.
The letter is written by her.
The letter had been written by her.
questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes "has been + past participle".

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: People speak English all over the world.
options: English was spoken all over the world.
English speaks all over the world.
English has been spoken all over the world.
English is spoken all over the world.

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: The technician is checking the cables.
options: The cables were checked by the technician.
The cables are checked by the technician.
The cables have been checked by the technician.
The cables are being checked by the technician.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes "are being + past participle".

questions.question: Change to the active voice: The window was broken by the storm.
options: The storm breaks the window.
The storm has broken the window.
The storm broke the window.
The storm was breaking the window.

questions.question: Change to the active voice: Has the file been sent by you?
options: Did you send the file?
Had you sent the file?
Have you sent the file?
Are you sending the file?
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive becomes present perfect active.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: He said, "I will help you."
options: He said that he will help you.
He said that I would help him.
He said that he would help me.
He said that he helps me.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: She said to me, "Where are you going?"
options: She asked me where I was going.
She told me where was I going.
She asked me where am I going.
She asked me that where I was going.
questions.explanation: A reported question takes statement order and the tense moves back.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: The teacher said, "The earth moves round the sun."
options: The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher told that the earth is moving round the sun.
The teacher said the earth will move round the sun.
questions.explanation: A universal truth keeps the present tense in reported speech.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: He said, "Alas! I have failed."
options: He exclaimed sadly that he had failed.
He said alas that he has failed.
He exclaimed that I had failed.
He exclaimed sadly that he has failed.
questions.explanation: An exclamation is reported with "exclaimed" and the tense moves back.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: She said to him, "Please wait here."
options: She said him to wait here.
She requested him to wait there.
She requested him wait here.
She requested that he waits here.
questions.explanation: A polite request is reported with "requested + object + to + verb"; "here" becomes "there".

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: "Don't make noise," said the teacher to the boys.
options: The teacher told the boys do not make noise.
The teacher forbade the boys to make noise.
The teacher said the boys not to make noise.
The teacher forbade the boys making noise.
questions.explanation: A negative command is reported with "forbade/told not to".

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: Do it now.
options: It is done now.
Let it be done now.
Let it done now.
It should do now.
questions.explanation: An imperative becomes "Let + object + be + past participle".

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: Did the manager sign the form?
options: Did the form sign by the manager?
Was the form signed by the manager?
Is the form signed by the manager?
Was the form being signed by the manager?
questions.explanation: Simple past question becomes "Was/Were ... + past participle?".

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: The students must obey the rules.
options: The rules must obeyed by the students.
The rules are obeyed by the students.
The rules must be obeyed by the students.
The rules must be obey by the students.
